items.title: Turnout at Israel's election has reached a record high at the halfway stage
items.summary: Almost 45% of the electorate had voted by 2 p.m., the highest share since such records began in 1973. The highly anticipated vote is expected to be a close-fought contest, and perhaps even a stalemate Follow below for all the latest on the Israeli election on October 27, 2026, and its aftermath: While security remained the dominant issue for Israeli voters, one topic was largely absent from the election campaign: a peace process with the Palestinians After years of conflict and failed negotiations, that debate has been pushed to the political margins Has Israeli society abandoned the idea of coexistence? Avraham Burg, an Israeli writer and former Speaker of the Israeli Parliament, shares his insights with DW To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Turnout in Israel's election keeps rising. It reached a record 44.9% by 2 p.m.

items.title: Co-ordinated cattle raids kill at least 72 people in South Sudan
items.summary: Cattle are a main source of wealth and pride for many communities in South Sudan At least 72 people have been killed during cattle raids in South Sudan's northern Warrap state, according to the regional government An unspecified number of cattle were taken and homes burnt during what was a "co-ordinated attack" on Monday involving two communities in Tonj North county, the state authorities said Such deadly violence is often part of a cycle of revenge attacks as cattle are a main source of wealth and pride for many communities and are also important as young men need them as dowries to get married Clashes over territory are also common across the country as it prepares to hold its first election since its independence in 2011 - delayed because of a brutal civil war The clashes occurred near the border of Warrap and Unity states in the area of Akop Payam, with some members from Lou Ariik community said to have attacked those from Apuk Padoch community William Wol Mayom Bol, Warrap state's information minister, said they followed deadly violence last Friday that claimed eight lives The…

items.title: Turnout so far highest on record as Israelis vote in pivotal election
items.summary: Watch: What does Israel's election mean for Gaza - and the world Turnout so far is at record levels, as Israelis vote in what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history Polling published on Friday suggests incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu is almost neck-and-neck with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot in the race to become prime minister But neither of their political blocs are projected to win the 61 seats needed to form a majority government - meaning weeks or months of political wrangling may lie ahead The campaign has been shaped by the issues of democracy and security, and the election is widely being seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's rule Many leading parties complained on Tuesday morning of alleged irregularities at polling stations across the country - but Israel's Central Election Committee (CEC) says there is no evidence of systematic tampering with ballot slips Israel's proportional representation system means governments have always been coalitions - and the race to power can, and has, produced unexpected alliances.

items.title: Nurse killed in attack while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
items.summary: A nurse has been killed and another health worker seriously injured in an attack as they were responding to an Ebola alert in north-eastern Democratic Republic of Congo The two were targeted by local youths who accused them of contaminating water sources and spreading the Ebola virus, according to the UN-backed Radio Okapi.
